thread:
sara: Heads up — we're seeing a recurring latency spike in eu-west dedicated pools starting ~08:12 UTC, correlating with a huge jump in outbound connections to kv-store-2 (10s of k RPS).
max: same, noticed LB error rates climb and tails for small gen requests went from 35ms -> 450ms.
kevin: ops-bot reported: Incident 2024-11-08T08:15 egress-saturation-eu-west. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT GW?
ops-bot: ALERT: egress-saturation-eu-west — SNAT port usage 99% on nat-gw-prod-eu2 for vpc-redwood-prod.
lila: If it's SNAT exhaustion, tenants with lots of short-lived TCP connections will hog ephemeral ports and cause timeouts for others (noisy neighbor).
sara: Logs show a pattern: thousands of 443 outbound short connects to kv-store-2 across multiple tenants. We have warm-pool traffic + per-tenant prefetchers doing reconnects. Sample flow: 
```
Aug 08 08:12:22 host-122 kube-proxy: conn track: src=10.3.x.x:59732 -> kv-store-2:443 CLOSE_WAIT
Aug 08 08:12:22 nat-gw: snat_alloc failed for 10.3.x.x:59732
```
max: Quick mitigation idea: enable per-tenant egress proxies (reuse connections) or increase NAT GW count temporarily. Both costy.
kevin: Agreed. Also we can do short-term egress policing to shape tenants that suddenly spike. Maybe implement an egress token bucket at our sidecar or envoy with a small penalty box for >X new connections/s.
lila: We already have an egress policy framework but not per-tenant new-conn limit. Would be a config change + small rollout.
sara: Cost check: adding a second NAT GW in eu-west is ~+$1200/mo plus data processing fees. Per-tenant proxies mean infra + engineering time but save NAT GW capex.
max: For immediate relief, I can flip a routing change to send heavy-tenants to dedicated nat-gw-2 owned by Dedicated lane for 1 hour. That should lower aggregate port pressure. Anyone object?
kevin: +1 but need to make sure routing respects tenant isolation flags. Put a guardrail: if nat-gw-2 SNAT >95%, revert.
ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: change-request #4512 — route tenants [acme-*, beta-*] -> nat-gw-2 (temp). Created by max.
sara: Also want telemetry — add metric: ephemeral_ports_in_use per nat-gw per 1m and per-tenant new_conn_rate. Set alert at 85% and 1500 new_conn/s.
lila: I'll open a PR for envoy filter to limit new conn bursts per tenant. Small patch, can ship to canary in eu2.
max: For long term we should consider connection pooling at the SDK level (keepalives) and NGW reuse: e.g., reuse outbound HTTP/2 multiplexing for kv-store interactions. That reduces ephemeral churn.
kevin: Agree, and evaluate whether we can move internal kv traffic to internal VPC endpoints to bypass NAT entirely for a subset of tenants (security review needed).
sara: FYI thermal-alarms were also reported on rack-11 earlier; just checked, those hosts were in warm-pool but not primary. Not sure if related but keep an eye.
infra-oncall: oncall running the nat-gw switch now. Will post when done.
ops-bot: RESOLVED: egress-saturation-eu-west — temporary routing change applied, SNAT usage dropped to 42% on nat-gw-prod-eu2. Monitoring for 30m.
max: Follow-ups: 1) telemetry PR 2) envoy new_conn limit rollout 3) SDK keepalive doc for customers 4) cost analysis for persistent nat-gw scaling. I'll make a checklist.
sara: Thanks team. Small note: include cost estimate for per-tenant proxies vs NAT GW scaling in the checklist.
lila: Will add to PR description.
kevin: Postmortem draft please in #postmortems once incident cools.
ops-bot: NOTE: if issue reappears, auto-escalate to infra-pager at 95% SNAT for >5m.
max: closing the loop here, will follow up with a short runbook for egress saturation scenarios.
